Cobordism experiment — the realizable image: results¶

What the re-run sweep shows once the realizable Dijkgraaf–Witten 2-boundary map image is no longer a single point. The twisted-cylinder builder (#193) grew the image from \(\{I_4\}\) to the full \(S_3\cong SL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\) of holonomy permutations; this experiment re-runs the labeled operation sweep against that enriched image and reports the now non-degenerate separating property. Companion to the runnable examples/cobordism/realizable_image_sweep.py; mirrors the bridge report (cobordism-bridge-report.md) and the realizability report (cobordism-realizability-report.md); grounds in the charter cobordism.md §5.

Verdict¶

An operation \(U\) on \(Z(T^2)=\mathbb{C}[H^1(T^2;\mathbb{Z}_2)]=\mathbb{C}^4\) is DW-realizable if and only if it is one of the six holonomy permutations — the permutation representation of a \(GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)=SL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\) automorphism of \(H^1(T^2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\), fixing the trivial class (index 0) and permuting the three non-trivial classes \(\{[a],[b],[a{+}b]\}=\{1,2,3\}\). The prior sweep (#191) found the realizable set was the single point \(\{I_4\}\), so the realizability-trend question was degenerate — every distinguishing property looked the same as “\(U=I_4\)”. With Cobordism.twistedCylinder the realizable set is now the 6-element group \(S_3\), and the separation is clean: of the 24 of \(S_4\)’s \(4\times4\) permutation matrices, exactly the 6 that fix index 0 are realizable; the other 18 are not. The discriminating property is no longer distance-to-\(I_4\) but distance-to-\(S_3\).

The enrichment: \(\{I_4\}\to S_3\)¶

The DW functor sends a cobordism \(W:T^2\to T^2\) to a linear map on \(Z(T^2)=\mathbb{C}^4\) (the flat-\(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-connection basis, classes indexed \(0=[\text{trivial}]\), \(1=[a]\), \(2=[b]\), \(3=[a{+}b]\), the BoundaryStateSpace::generatorIndex convention \(i\mapsto 2^i\)). With only the order-preserving product cylinder available — the one glue/selfGlue produce — the realizable image collapsed to the single map \(I_4\). Cobordism.twistedCylinder( \Sigma,\varphi) threads the two boundary copies of \(\Sigma\) through a finite-order simplicial automorphism \(\varphi\) instead of the identity, so the interior monodromy is \(\varphi\) and DijkgraafWitten.map() returns the permutation \(\varphi\) induces on the holonomy classes. Two generators close the group:

  • the coordinate swap \(\varphi:(u,v)\mapsto(v,u)\) on the 9-vertex product torus \(T^2=\texttt{SimplicialProduct}(\partial\Delta^2,\partial\Delta^2)\) — the transposition \((1\,2)\) that exchanges \([a]\leftrightarrow[b]\) and fixes \([0],[a{+}b]\) (its \(\bmod\,2\) reduction is the modular \(S=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\));

  • the multiplier \(\varphi:i\mapsto 2i\pmod 7\) on the 7-vertex Möbius torus — the order-3 rotation \((1\,2\,3)\) that cycles \([a]\to[b]\to[a{+}b]\) and fixes \([0]\).

The two surfaces differ (9 vs 7 vertices), but both maps fix the trivial-class index 0 and act on the same three non-trivial indices \(\{1,2,3\}\) in DijkgraafWitten.computeBoundary’s class order, so they compose. Generated by matrix multiplication, \(\langle\,\mathrm{DW(swap)},\mathrm{DW(3\text{-}cycle)}\, \rangle\) closes to a group of exactly 6 elements: a transposition and a 3-cycle on the same 3-element set generate the full \(S_3\). That group is the realizable image.

Why \(S_3\) is the full symmetric group (the separator)¶

The three non-trivial holonomy classes are precisely the three non-zero vectors of \((\mathbb{Z}_2)^2\): \([a]=(1,0)\), \([b]=(0,1)\), \([a{+}b]=(1,1)\). A permutation \(\sigma\) of these three is induced by a \(GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\)-linear map iff \(\sigma([a{+}b])=\sigma([a])+\sigma([b])\) — but this is automatic: any two distinct non-zero vectors of \((\mathbb{Z}_2)^2\) are linearly independent, hence a basis, so \(\sigma([a])+\sigma([b])\) is the unique remaining non-zero vector, which is exactly \(\sigma([a{+}b])\). Therefore every permutation of the three non-trivial classes is \(GF(2)\)-linear, and the permutation representation \(GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\to S_3\) is an isomorphism onto the full symmetric group. This is why the realizable image is the entire \(S_3\) and not a proper subgroup, and it hands us the clean separator:

\[ U\text{ is DW-realizable}\iff U\text{ is a }0/1\text{ permutation matrix that fixes the trivial class}\iff U\in\text{the }GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\text{ rep on }\mathbb{C}[H^1]. \]

In the sweep this is the only candidate property that separates the realizable operations from the rest with no false positives and no false negatives (the is_holonomy_perm row above: \(P\&\overline{W}=0\), \(\overline{P}\&W=0\)). The weaker properties leak: being a permutation admits the 18 that move index 0; fixing the trivial class admits diagonal sign matrices; being diagonal and flux-commuting miss the off-diagonal swaps entirely.

The gap is governed by distance-to-\(S_3\), not distance-to-\(I_4\)¶

Because \(I_4\in S_3\), the new metric never exceeds the old one, \(\texttt{gap\_to\_S3}(U)=\min_{g\in S_3}\lVert U-g\rVert\le\lVert U-I_4\rVert= \texttt{gap\_to\_I4}(U)\), and for the realizable maps other than \(I_4\) the two diverge sharply: the swap sits at \(\texttt{gap\_to\_I4}=2\) but \(\texttt{gap\_to\_S3} =0\). The old “near-\(I_4\)” test is now visibly degenerate — it flags only the seven copies of the identity in the families and misses the other twelve realizable maps (the near_I4 row: 7 caught, 12 missed). Distance-to-\(S_3\) is the metric that tracks realizability.

The gates row is the instructive surprise: SWAP (\(=\) the swap \((1\,2)\)) and CNOT (\(=\) the transposition \((2\,3)\) on the holonomy classes) are realizable because they happen to be holonomy permutations fixing the trivial class, while CZ, iSWAP, CPHASE, and the Hadamards are not — realizability is a property of the holonomy action, indifferent to the operation’s name in the qubit gate set.

Method¶

The example is pure orchestration of the merged, separately-tested classes — Cobordism.twistedCylinder + DijkgraafWitten.map (the realizable maps), ChoiJamiolkowski.transitionAmplitude and BoundaryStateSpace.state / DijkgraafWitten.amplitude (the genuine operation reading). The recipe:

  1. Build the realizable set. DW(swap) from the 9-vertex product torus and DW(3-cycle) from the 7-vertex Möbius torus (the #193 fixtures, reused so the two generators share the holonomy-class indexing), then close the matrix group by breadth-first multiplication and certify it is the 6-element \(S_3\) — every element a \(0/1\) permutation fixing index 0 and \(GF(2)\)-linear, and the set equal to exactly the \(S_4\) permutations that fix index 0.

  2. Read each operation through the machinery. \(\langle e_i|U|e_j\rangle\) via ChoiJamiolkowski.transitionAmplitude over the holonomy basis reconstructs the \(4\times4\) matrix; the product cylinder’s metric-free state sum read through DijkgraafWitten.amplitude on BoundaryStateSpace.state is \(I_4\), anchoring the identity reading in two independent code paths.

  3. Score. \(\texttt{gap\_to\_S3}=\min_{g\in S_3}\lVert U-g\rVert\) and the old \(\texttt{gap\_to\_I4}=\lVert U-I_4\rVert\), with \(\texttt{realizable}:= \texttt{gap\_to\_S3}<10^{-7}\), plus the candidate separating properties.

  4. Discriminate. The full 24 of \(S_4\)’s permutation matrices are the discriminating family; cross-tabulate each candidate property against the realizable verdict to find the one that separates cleanly.

The realizable closure and the \(GF(2)\)-linearity of every realized map are re-derived independently in tests/cobordism/test_realizable_image_python.py (a separate code path from the example), which also checks the genuine-machinery reading reconstructs \(U\) and that the committed example self-verifies.

Key findings¶

  1. The realizable image is exactly \(S_3\cong GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\). The swap and the 3-cycle DW maps generate, by matrix multiplication, a group of exactly six \(0/1\) permutation matrices — the full symmetric group on the three non-trivial holonomy classes, fixing the trivial one. The old realizable set \(\{I_4\}\) is the identity element of this group.

  2. The 6-of-24 separation is clean. Of the 24 of \(S_4\)’s permutation matrices exactly the 6 that fix index 0 are realizable; the 18 that move the trivial class are not. No operation is misclassified by the holonomy-permutation property.

  3. The separator is \(GF(2)\)-linearity of the holonomy action. Realizable \(\iff\) \(U\) is a \(0/1\) permutation fixing the trivial class \(\iff\) \(U\) is the permutation rep of a \(GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\) automorphism of \(H^1(T^2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\). Because every permutation of the three non-zero vectors of \((\mathbb{Z}_2)^2\) is automatically linear, the realizable image is the full \(S_3\).

  4. Distance-to-\(S_3\) replaces distance-to-\(I_4\). The old near-\(I_4\) metric is degenerate against the enriched image — it catches only the identity copies and misses the twelve other realizable maps. The gap for a non-realizable operation is now governed by its distance to \(S_3\).

  5. Realizability is a holonomy property, not a gate-set property. SWAP and CNOT are realizable; CZ, iSWAP, the Hadamards, the DFT, and Haar-random \(U(4)\) are not — entirely determined by whether the operation permutes the holonomy classes fixing the trivial one. This answers the realizability question the prior sweep left open: the discrete DW image is the \(GL(2,\mathbb{Z}_2)\) holonomy-permutation group, period.

Conventions¶

  • Holonomy classes index \(0=[\text{trivial}]\), \(1=[a]\), \(2=[b]\), \(3=[a{+}b]\); the spectral generator \(i\) maps to class \(2^i\) (BoundaryStateSpace::generatorIndex).

  • Operators are flat row-major; \(\mathrm{vec}(U)\) is the row-major flatten (ChoiJamiolkowski.vectorize).

  • \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is the Frobenius norm; \(\texttt{gap\_to\_S3}=\min_{g\in S_3} \lVert U-g\rVert\), \(\texttt{realizable}:=\texttt{gap\_to\_S3}<10^{-7}\).

  • The DW maps are read metric-free (topology + cocycle only); both the trivial and sign cocycles give the same permutation (the mod-2 cup cube vanishes on the cylinder).

  • Seeded and reproducible; the 10-CPU cap is honored (thread env set at launch).

Reproduce¶

pip install -e ".[dev]"
python examples/cobordism/realizable_image_sweep.py        # the tables above
python -m pytest tests/cobordism/test_realizable_image_python.py

The raw full sweep table (all 229 rows, CSV + Markdown) defaults to /tmp/cobordism/realizable_image_sweep.{csv,md} and is not committed — the script is the committed artifact. Attach it to the issue/PR to pin a result.
